newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Sep oil trade gap $28 mln, same as yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Sep oil trade gap $28 mln, same as yr ago.

text.p: Peru's oil and derivatives trade deficit was $28 million, virtually unchanged from the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Tuesday.
The oil and derivatives deficit in the first nine months was $168 million, up slightly from $167 million in the same period last year, the bank said in its weekly report.

September's imports of oil and derivatives were $49 million, up from $47 million in the same month last year. Exports in September rose to $21 million, up from $20 million in the same month last year.
In the first nine months of the year, imports of oil and derivatives rose 26.1 percent to $435 million. Exports rose 49.6 percent to $267 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Peru's oil deficit swelled 134 percent to $323.2 million in 1995 compared with $138 million the previous year, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
